title: expo-router 57 rejects react-navigation: drop @react-navigation/* from the app
description: Missed in the SDK 57 realignment. Dev build compiled and installed fine, then Metro returned HTTP 500 on /index.bundle: 'As of SDK 56, expo-router is no longer compatible with react-navigation' (thrown by @expo/cli withMetroMultiPlatform.js:608). expo-router 57 vendors its own navigation at expo-router/build/react-navigation/ and its Metro resolver hard-fails if @react-navigation/* is resolvable from the project. Single offending import chain: components/haptic-tab.tsx -> @react-navigation/elements (PlatformPressable) and @react-navigation/bottom-tabs (BottomTabBarButtonProps), reached via app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx tabBarButton. Fix: rewrote haptic-tab.tsx on plain react-native Pressable (expo-router's vendored PlatformPressable is itself marked @deprecated 'copy the component into your codebase'), press feedback set to opacity 0.8 per docs/design-language.md:383; removed @react-navigation/bottom-tabs, /elements and /native from package.json (zero remaining source references); removed the ComponentProps cast the earlier pass had added in app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx, which was papering over this same incompatibility as a type-drift issue.
design: Root cause vs symptom: the earlier realignment pass treated the pressColor ColorValue-vs-string mismatch between expo-router's vendored BottomTabBarButtonProps and the real @react-navigation/elements as upstream type drift and cast around it. That mismatch WAS this bug - two different navigation implementations in one tree. Removing react-navigation removed both the runtime failure and the type mismatch, so the cast is gone.
acceptance_criteria: Metro serves /index.bundle with HTTP 200 for android, ios and web; tsc --noEmit and npm run lint clean; @react-navigation unresolvable from project root.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: android/ios/web bundles all return HTTP 200 from a clean Metro; tsc and lint clean.

title: Patch remaining fixable vulns: @vercel/node 5.9.8 + xmldom override

Add package.json overrides { '@xmldom/xmldom': '^0.8.13' } to clear 5 high xmldom advisories (all <0.8.13) reached via @expo/plist <- @bacons/xcode <- @bacons/apple-targets; @expo/plist requests ^0.8.8 so this is a patch-level nudge inside its declared range. Repo has no existing overrides/resolutions/patches. Then rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install for a clean tree.
design: uuid (moderate, <11.1.1) deliberately NOT overridden: consumers @bacons/xcode and xcode want ^8.3.2 and ^7.0.3, uuid 9 removed the default export, so forcing 11 breaks iOS prebuild for a moderate bounds check.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit shows no high entries outside the image-size/metro cluster; api/_lib/http.ts and api/_lib/router.ts typecheck against @vercel/node 5.x types.
close_reason: Closed

title: Expo SDK 57 dependency realignment + vulnerability remediation

Realign the whole dependency set to Expo SDK 57 canonical versions, fix every vulnerability that has a published fix, and repair the resulting source breakage. title: Web: all API calls fail with Illegal invocation (fetchImpl called as method)
description: On web, expo/fetch is the unbound globalThis.fetch. utils/api-client-core.ts sendRequest calls deps.fetchImpl(...) as a method, binding this=deps, so Chrome throws 'Failed to execute fetch on Window: Illegal invocation'. Every web API call dies before hitting the network; signed-in web users only see the 'Could not load your account' card. Fix: call fetchImpl as a free function + regression test.
close_reason: Fixed: fetchImpl called as free function in utils/api-client-core.ts + regression test

title: Workout and pushup-challenge response envelopes never parse; pushes loop forever

Affects GET/POST/PATCH /api/workouts and both /api/pushup-challenge verbs. Pre-existing; conflict auto-resolution just made it visible.

title: AOD notification set advance is lost; any 404 deletes the local row

Process death then loses the set and the screen rehydrates stale. (B) db/sync.ts maps every ApiNotFoundError to SyncNotFoundError and the engine answers with removeClean, so any infra 404 deletes local rows.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stop draining the Live Activity action outbox when no JS listener is attached
description:
apps/mobile/modules/live-update-notification/ios/LiveUpdateNotificationModule.swift's onActionPosted() (currently lines 220-230) calls LiveUpdateSharedStore.drainPendingAction() — which removeObject's the App Group record — and THEN sendEvent. If nothing is subscribed yet, the durable record is destroyed and the event is dropped. The outbox is a single slot, so that tap is gone for good.

This is reachable in normal use: the root subscription in app/_layout.tsx is inside a useEffect gated on 'if (!user) return', so there is a real window at launch/sign-in where the Darwin observer (registered in OnCreate) exists but no JS listener does.

Work:
1. Add 'private var hasListeners = false' to LiveUpdateNotificationModule.
2. In definition(), next to Events("onNotificationAction"):
     OnStartObserving("onNotificationAction") { self.hasListeners = true }
     OnStopObserving("onNotificationAction")  { self.hasListeners = false }
   These factories exist in SDK 57 with an optional event-name first parameter — see node_modules/expo-modules-core/ios/Api/Factories/ObjectFactories.swift:47.
3. In onActionPosted(), add 'guard hasListeners else { return }' BEFORE the drain, so an unobserved tap stays in the outbox.

Do NOT change the show() dedupe at lines 93-97. Once pump-pal-byyv.8 removes the intent's StoredState writes, that dedupe is the single correct choke point again and is what kills the keystroke firehose from byyv.1/byyv.2.
design: An unobserved tap now survives in the App Group outbox and is picked up by the existing cold-start drainPendingAction() path in src/lib/live-update-notification-actions.ios.ts:66. No new foreground-replay machinery is needed: once a listener IS registered, sendEvent enqueues on the JS runtime and survives a starved JS thread on its own. Uses the platform's own listener lifecycle rather than hand-rolled bookkeeping.
acceptance_criteria: onActionPosted returns early without draining when no listener is attached. OnStartObserving/OnStopObserving toggle hasListeners. show()'s dedupe block is unchanged. bun --cwd=apps/mobile run test:live-activity-config passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove the optimistic Activity push from the Live Activity App Intents
description:
apps/mobile/targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift currently makes the App Intent a SECOND writer of LiveUpdateSharedStore.StoredState: performSetAction advances completedSets, calls saveState, and calls activity.update via pushOptimisticState before JS has validated anything. This re-broke the invariant pump-pal-ks2l's design note set ("Do NOT re-add optimistic local updates").

Failure it causes: each button carries expectedCompletedSets = context.state.completedSets. The intent guard validates it against StoredState; the JS guard (matchesExpectedCompletedSets in src/lib/wear-action-task.ts) validates it against session.rows. Once one tap advances StoredState without JS applying it, the two diverge permanently — the intent accepts every later tap, JS rejects every later tap. Observed symptom: only the first Complete set works.

Work:
1. Delete optimisticActions(...) and pushOptimisticState(...) (currently lines 12-42).
2. Delete the '// ponytail: optimistic redraw' block at the end of performSetAction (currently lines 71-99). performSetAction collapses back to: three guards -> writePendingAction -> postActionDarwinNotification.
3. Drop 'import ActivityKit' — nothing references Activity/ActivityContent afterwards.
4. Keep all six NSLog guard rejections. They are the only device-side way to tell 'intent never ran' from 'ran and rejected'.
5. Add above 'import AppIntents':

// The app target gets this file via plugins/with-live-activity-intents.js, where these
// types come from the LiveUpdateNotification pod (useFrameworks: static makes it a real
// Swift module). In the widget extension the pod is absent and the same types come from
// this folder's own copies, so canImport is false and the import is skipped.
#if canImport(LiveUpdateNotification)
import LiveUpdateNotification
#endif

title: Move Live Activity dedupe into the native ActivityKit choke point
description:
See parent pump-pal-byyv for the full root cause.

The JS lastPayloadKey dedupe in workout-notification.ios.ts cannot see the optimistic Activity.update that WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift:99 performs, because that runs in the host-app process path before JS is involved. The App Group store (LiveUpdateSharedStore) is the ONLY record both writers touch, so it is the only place a correct dedupe can live.

CHANGE 1 - apps/mobile/modules/live-update-notification/ios/LiveUpdateNotificationModule.swift, show() at :79-121:
After building contentState and BEFORE saveState / the Task { @MainActor } block, early-return true when the store already holds this exact content:

    if let stored = LiveUpdateSharedStore.loadState(),
       stored.workoutId == payload.workoutId,
       stored.asContentState == contentState {
      return true
    }

WorkoutActivityAttributes.ContentState is already Codable, Hashable (WorkoutActivityAttributes.swift:26), so == is free. Do NOT modify WorkoutActivityAttributes.swift - its byte-equality assertion in live-activity-config.test.js:38-42 must keep passing.

CHANGE 2 - move the existing beginActivityOperation() call to AFTER this guard. Today it is the first line of show(); leaving it above the guard would let an unchanged redraw bump the generation counter and cancel an in-flight real update.

CHANGE 3 - add an asContentState computed property to LiveUpdateSharedStore.StoredState returning WorkoutActivityAttributes.ContentState(completedSets:totalSets:detail:segments:actions:). This must be added IDENTICALLY to BOTH copies of the file:
  - apps/mobile/modules/live-update-notification/ios/LiveUpdateSharedStore.swift
  - apps/mobile/targets/widget/LiveUpdateSharedStore.swift
They are separate build units (CocoaPods module target vs @bacons/apple-targets widget extension) kept in sync by hand. They currently differ only in their header comment.

DO NOT change the intents from LiveActivityIntent to AppIntent. Activity<T>.activities is empty in the widget-extension process.

SCOPE: the three Swift files named above. Do not touch JS in this bead.

title: Gate Live Activity redraws on app background (kill the keystroke firehose)
description:
The single biggest source of ActivityKit budget burn. See parent pump-pal-byyv for the full root cause.

apps/mobile/app/active-workout.tsx:430-444 runs a 100ms-debounced showWorkoutNotification effect keyed on [exercises, effectiveWorkoutName, sessionId, initializing, startedAt]. Because the payload detail line is currentSetDetail() - the next set exercise label + reps + weight - EVERY KEYSTROKE in a weight/reps/name field produces a distinct payload, defeats the existing dedupe, and spends one Activity.update.

iOS hides a Live Activity Dynamic Island presentation while its own app is frontmost, so every one of those redraws is budget spent on pixels nobody can see.

CHANGE:
- Gate the debounced showWorkoutNotification call on AppState.currentState !== "active".
- Add an AppState "change" listener that flushes exactly one redraw on the transition to background/inactive, so the island is correct the moment it becomes visible.
- Raise the debounce from 100 to 1000 ms. Its only stated job (see its own comment at :425-430) is coalescing keystroke bursts. The button paths do not depend on it for first paint: the intent optimistic push (WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift:99) and wear-action-task.ts:63 both redraw immediately.

Use react-native AppState.addEventListener("change", ...) directly. Do not add a hook or a new dependency.

SCOPE: apps/mobile/app/active-workout.tsx only. Do not touch the Swift side or wear-action-task.ts in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Typing in weight/reps/exercise-name fields while the app is foregrounded triggers zero calls into showWorkoutNotification.

- The AppState listener and the debounce timer are both torn down on unmount; the background flush cannot fire after the session ends or after navigation away.

title: iOS Live Activity buttons degrade then stop: ActivityKit update-budget exhaustion
description:
Interactive buttons on the iOS Live Activity respond slowly, degrade over the course of a workout, and eventually stop responding. Android/Pixel has no equivalent problem.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a workout on iOS (iOS 17+, Live Activities enabled).
2. Background the app so the Dynamic Island / Lock Screen presentation is visible.
3. Tap "Complete set" repeatedly, returning to the app between sets to type weight/reps.
4. Work through a full workout. Each tap takes progressively longer to move the count; late in the workout the buttons stop responding at all.

Console.app filtered to ActivityKit shows bursts of 16+ consecutive "[ActivityKit] Updating content for activity <same-id>" lines plus "[BoardServices] [S:n] Error received: Connection invalidated." scene teardowns.

## Root Cause
ActivityKit meters local Activity.update() calls against a slowly-refilling per-app budget. Over budget, the system first delays and then drops updates. Progressive degradation ending in "stops working" is that signature exactly.

Android does not hit this because NotificationManager.notify(NOTIFICATION_ID, n) is a free, synchronous, idempotent in-place replace; workout-notification.android.ts re-posts on every call with no dedupe at all. iOS cannot copy that literally, only the SHAPE: one authoritative snapshot, one post per real change.

Where the updates come from:
1. Keystrokes (DOMINANT). detail = currentSetDetail() = next set exercise label + reps + weight. Every character typed into a weight/reps/name field changes exercises, re-runs the 100ms debounce effect at app/active-workout.tsx:430-444, and fires one Activity.update. Hundreds per workout. This is why it gets worse as it goes.
2. Optimistic push inside the intent, targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift:99 - 1 per tap.
3. JS authoritative redraw, src/lib/wear-action-task.ts:63 - 1 per tap, differing from the optimistic state only in detail/segments.
4. force:true correction redraws at wear-action-task.ts:49 and :56, which exist SOLELY to defeat the JS dedupe - 1 extra on every stale/no-op tap.
5. Debounce effect re-firing after subscribeSession -> setExercises (active-workout.tsx:415-424).

Why the existing JS lastPayloadKey dedupe (pump-pal-jcgl, closed) helped but did not fix it: it is structurally unable to see the intent optimistic Activity.update, which runs in a different process before JS is involved. The JS follow-up therefore always looks new.

## Hard Constraint - DO NOT UNDO
CompleteSetIntent/UncompleteSetIntent/FinishWorkoutIntent must stay LiveActivityIntent (host-app process). Activity<T>.activities is EMPTY in the widget-extension process, so a plain AppIntent could not call Activity.update at all (Apple forum thread 735382). The plugins/with-live-activity-intents.js copy-into-both-targets setup is likewise required.

## Goal
At most 1 Activity.update per real, user-visible state change, with the keystroke firehose eliminated entirely. Button behaviour unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: All five child beads closed. Device verification: tapping Complete set ~10x with the app backgrounded produces at most 2 ActivityKit update log lines per tap and no BoardServices teardown bursts, and taps stay responsive for a full workout. Typing in weight/reps fields while foregrounded produces ZERO ActivityKit update lines.

title: Rebuild the iOS Live Activity layout on Android's ProgressStyle
description:
The iOS Live Activity layout is unfinished and does not read like the Pixel Live Update the Android module produces. The segment bar is 4pt with an off-grid 3pt gap and no position tracker - the one element that makes Android's Notification.ProgressStyle recognizable. The minimal presentation renders a string like '12/24' inside a ~24pt circle.

All of this is apps/mobile/targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivity.swift.

TOKENS (all already used by the Android module; no new colors, no gradient, no glass):
  complete #e54242 | current #fbbf24 | pending #666666 | chip secondary white@12%
  radius 14 buttons, capsule track | spacing 4/8/12/16 | system font, monospacedDigit() on every number

SegmentBar - the signature element. Keep the GeometryReader proportional-width math, it is correct. Change:
  - bar height 4 -> 6; RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 2) -> Capsule(); gap 3 -> 4
  - add a tracker pip at completedSets/totalSets of the full track width: a 10pt white circle with a 2pt #0f0f0f ring so it reads over any segment color. Hidden when totalSets == 0. This is Android's ProgressStyle tracker and the one thing iOS is missing.
  - container height 10 (pip) with the bar centered so the pip does not clip
  - keep the existing accessibilityElement(children: .ignore) + label/value block

ActionButtons - real chips. Extract one ActionChip view: Text at .subheadline.weight(.semibold), lineLimit(1), minimumScaleFactor(0.85), .frame(maxWidth: .infinity).frame(height: 38), .buttonStyle(.plain), .background(prominent ? accent : Color.white.opacity(0.12), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14, style: .continuous)), .foregroundStyle(.white).

Arrangements, driven by context.state.actions (the model emits exactly these, see src/lib/workout-notification-model.ts:96-104):
  ['completeSet']                      -> one full-width accent chip
  ['completeSet','uncompleteSet']      -> two equal-width chips; Complete accent, Undo secondary
  ['finishWorkout','uncompleteSet']    -> Finish workout full-width accent; Undo set BELOW it as a plain centered text button, no chip background
  []                                    -> nothing

  row 1: title (headline) ......... elapsed timer (headline mono)
  row 2: detail (#888) ............ '3/9' count (mono #888)
  row 3: full-bleed segment track + pip
  row 4: action chips
The set count moves OFF the button row and onto the detail row's trailing edge, so it sits beside the label it counts and the track runs full-bleed - that is what makes the Pixel bar read as a bar. title: Compile the Live Activity intents into the iOS app target
description:
Live Activity buttons do nothing on iOS. CompleteSetIntent/UncompleteSetIntent/FinishWorkoutIntent conform to LiveActivityIntent, which iOS performs in the APP's process (that is the whole reason the protocol exists instead of plain AppIntent). All three types exist only in apps/mobile/targets/widget/, which compiles into the TimberWidget extension. The app target has no such type, so the tap resolves to nothing and returns silently.

Work:
1. New apps/mobile/plugins/with-live-activity-intents.js, following the shape of the existing apps/mobile/plugins/with-notifee-maven.js:
   - withDangerousMod(['ios', ...]) copies targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift to ios/Timber/WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift on every prebuild, so there is one source of truth and it cannot drift the way the two LiveUpdateSharedStore.swift copies already do.
   - withXcodeProject calls IOSConfig.XcodeUtils.addBuildSourceFileToGroup({ filepath: 'Timber/WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift', groupName: 'Timber', project: config.modResults }), guarded so a re-run does not add a duplicate build file.
2. Register './plugins/with-live-activity-intents' in apps/mobile/app.json expo.plugins, AFTER '@bacons/apple-targets'.
3. apps/mobile/targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift: fix the header comment that claims the intent 'runs insulated in the Live Activity own process' - it runs in the APP's process, and that wrong comment is what the missing app-target membership followed from. Add an NSLog on each guard rejection naming which condition failed (no stored state / workoutId mismatch / expected-count mismatch); every failure path is currently a silent return, so a device run cannot tell 'never ran' from 'ran and rejected'. Drop the now-unused import ActivityKit.

The intent's LiveUpdateSharedStore reference resolves against the app target's own copy, which the pod already provides at modules/live-update-notification/ios/LiveUpdateSharedStore.swift - same appGroupId, same UserDefaults keys, one container.
design:
Config-plugin route chosen over copying the intents file into modules/live-update-notification/ios/. The podspec already globs ios/**/*.swift, but app.json sets useFrameworks:static so the pod is a separate Swift module, and AppIntents metadata extraction runs per-target - the app's Metadata.appintents may not pick up types from a static-framework pod, which would silently still do nothing. Apple's documented arrangement is that the intent file is a member of both targets; the plugin produces exactly that.

Do NOT re-add optimistic local updates (activity.update / saveState / activity.end) to the intents. Those were removed deliberately so a force-quit tap cannot claim data persisted (IOS_LOCAL_PREVIEW.md:98-103). Once the intent lives in the app target, iOS background-launches the app to run it, so a backgrounded tap reaches a live JS runtime and redraws for real.
acceptance_criteria: plugins/with-live-activity-intents.js exists and is idempotent; app.json lists it after @bacons/apple-targets; the intents file's process comment is correct, each guard branch logs, and import ActivityKit is gone. bun run lint and bun run typecheck pass.

title: Epic: Direct Firestore clients with a privileged Cloudflare Worker
description:
Outcome: native clients keep UID-scoped SQLite as their sole UI source of truth and sync safe operations directly through Firestore REST; web performs safe online-only Firestore access; a liftable Hono Cloudflare Worker handles only secret-bearing, cross-user, privileged, and abuse-sensitive operations. Firebase Auth, App Check, strict Security Rules, split trust-domain documents, and the existing @timber/contract domain DTOs uphold the contract.

Execution policy:
1. Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/purpose.md, docs/design-language.md when touching UI, docs/data-model/README.md, and every child bead before editing.
2. Use graphify before raw codebase exploration and run graphify update . after code changes.
3. Claim and complete ready children in dependency order; close only when acceptance criteria pass.
4. Optimize for the simplest correct implementation: reuse current REST codecs, repositories, SQLite/outbox, schemas, and API domain logic; avoid generic abstractions, broad rewrites, and extra infrastructure.
5. Preserve unrelated dirty work. Do not commit, pull, push, deploy, rotate secrets, mutate remote Firebase/Cloudflare configuration, or run production builds.
6. Use focused tests, type checks, rules emulator checks, and source inspection. Record remote-only deployment/App Check enforcement steps as explicit human gates.
7. Keep apps/api liftable with @timber/contract as its only workspace dependency.

Scope: transport-neutral contract helpers; trust-domain Firestore migration; strict rules/indexes and emulator tests; direct Firestore REST repositories for native and web; offline outbox conflict/error behavior; Hono Worker privileged routes with Firebase Auth and App Check; obsolete route retirement; docs, observability, migration tooling, preview/production rollout and rollback.

Non-goals: replacing Firebase Auth; Firestore SDK persistence on native; IndexedDB persistence on web; changing product UX; App Store/Play Store submission; automatically deploying or changing remote services.
design: Trust boundary: exact Security Rules authorize owner-safe direct Firestore operations; the Worker is not a generic Firestore proxy. Native remains local-first with opaque Firestore updateTime versions and one local-wins conflict retry. Web is online-only. Split users/{uid} data so injuries become per-item documents and server-managed quota/push fields move under private subdocuments. Require Firebase ID tokens and App Check on privileged Worker routes. Use a coordinated cutover with additive migration first, verified client adoption, then legacy cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are complete or explicitly human-gated; safe native/web flows bypass the Worker; native offline behavior survives process death and reconnect; strict rules and query constraints pass emulator tests; privileged routes enforce Auth plus App Check and preserve invariants; migration is idempotent and verified; docs match the deployed-target architecture; lightweight local quality gates pass; remote deployment/enforcement steps remain clearly documented and unexecuted unless separately authorized.
notes: All 11 children completed locally. Final focused gates passed: workspace typecheck, contract/API suites, direct Firestore transport + native sync/outbox/initial-sync checks, migration test, isolation guards, direct-boundary guard, and diff check. The Firestore emulator re-run remains a documented JDK-21 environment gate; no remote deployment, enforcement, migration, secret rotation, or cleanup was performed.

title: bun install: bunfig, lockfile cut, trustedDependencies
description:

2. BEFORE deleting anything, snapshot installed native dep versions:
   node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const d of Object.keys(require("./apps/mobile/package.json").dependencies)) try{console.log(d, JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(`node_modules/${d}/package.json`)).version)}catch{}' | sort > /tmp/before.txt
3. rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && bun install. Re-run the snippet into /tmp/after.txt and diff. Report every moved version. Pin back in package.json any moved expo*, react-native*, @notifee/*, or firebase version rather than accepting it silently.
4. Run 'bun pm untrusted'. Add whatever it reports to a root trustedDependencies array and re-run bun install. Known postinstall users in the current tree: esbuild, protobufjs, unrs-resolver, @firebase/util.
5. Leave 'overrides' alone (bun honours it). Confirm with 'bun pm why undici' and 'bun pm why minimatch'.
6. .gitignore needs no change. bun.lock stays tracked.

title: Implement manifest-based sync and versioned mutations
description: Add the server sync primitives required by the native offline client. Expose an authoritative per-user manifest of entity IDs and opaque versions, plus bounded pull/download support. Ensure all domain mutations accept baseVersion and return the resulting version. A stale mutation must preserve the remote copy and return a 409 containing the canonical remote payload/version; repeated creates, updates, and deletes must safely detect already-applied desired state.
design: Derive opaque versions from Firestore DocumentSnapshot updateTime or an equally authoritative server value. Prefer a full authoritative manifest for v1 because legacy direct clients may write during the grace period and would bypass an incremental log. Clean local records absent from the manifest may be removed; dirty missing records become conflicts. Define pagination/size limits.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest includes every synchronizable entity and detects legacy direct-client edits/deletes; pull is bounded and ownership-scoped; mutations return versions and use baseVersion atomically; stale, duplicate, deleted, and retry scenarios have tests; contract remains compatible with the offline epic.
notes:
Implemented sync manifest/pull. New: api/sync/{manifest,pull}.ts, api/_lib/store/sync.ts. Also added the missing shared/api-contract.ts SyncableKind type export (syncableKind existed as a zod enum but had no z.infer'd TS type -- needed it for sync.ts's groupByKind typing; purely additive, not a breaking contract change).

Design: v1 full authoritative manifest per the epic's own note (legacy direct-Firestore clients can still write during the grace period and would bypass an incremental log). GET /api/sync/manifest paginates over workouts (bounded, cursor via createdAt, same cursor mechanics as .3's listWorkouts) and additionally emits profile/injury/pushupChallenge entries -- but ONLY on the first page (no cursor) since those are cheap bounded per-user singletons and emitting them on every page would duplicate them across a multi-page walk. Injuries and profile share the user doc's updateTime as their version (they aren't independently versioned entities -- same tradeoff already made in .3/.4's injury/profile routes).

POST /api/sync/pull batches by kind via the pure, unit-tested groupByKind() so N requested injury ids cost one users/{uid} read, not N. Ownership is enforced by reusing .3's getOwnedWorkout, which throws 404 on a uid mismatch -- pull.ts catches that and folds it into  rather than a 403/error, so requesting someone else's workout id neither leaks data nor confirms/denies its existence.

Tests (all passing): test:api-sync (groupByKind bucketing, empty-input safety), plus the full existing suite (api-isolation/api-contract/api-rest/workouts/injuries/account/catalog/pushup/http/ai-model/ai-quota) and tsc --noEmit clean. This closes out the last of the CRUD-and-sync beads (.3/.4/.5/.7). Remaining: .6 already closed earlier; .8 (isolation/integration/observability/cold-start -- the Preview cold-start p95 gate needs an actual deploy, which is outside this sandbox) and .9 (rollout docs, explicitly human-gated for the production/rules cutover).

title: Make AI routing fully environment-controlled

Require only the selected provider's key and reject unsupported provider/model/reasoning combinations with actionable startup/config errors.

vercel:ai-sdk,vercel:env-vars
design: Use AI_PROVIDER=google|openai, AI_MODEL, AI_REASONING_EFFORT. Portable reasoning values are provider-default, none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh; allow max only when the selected direct provider supports it. Client requests choose an operation, never provider/model/effort. Preserve quotas, structured outputs, abort/timeout behavior, and redacted logs.

title: Implement catalog and pushup-challenge domain routes
description: Implement the exercise catalog read/pending-submission routes and pushup challenge read/write route. Preserve curated versus pending-review catalog semantics, challenge history/streak/daily-name data, and existing authorization constraints. Keep global catalog reads appropriately cacheable without allowing private user data to enter shared caches.
design: Pending exercise submissions are authenticated and server-attribute createdBy from the token. Use explicit cache headers/ETags only where safe. Return opaque versions for user-owned challenge state.
acceptance_criteria: All audited catalog and pushup Firestore calls have API coverage; pending submissions cannot spoof creator/status; challenge updates support baseVersion/conflicts and idempotent retries; catalog responses do not leak private data; focused route tests pass.
notes:
Implemented catalog + pushup-challenge domain routes. New: api/catalog/{index,pending}.ts, api/pushup-challenge/index.ts, api/_lib/store/{catalog,pushup-challenge}.ts.

Catalog read (GET /api/catalog) ports utils/exercise-catalog.ts loadCatalog()'s filter exactly (schemaVersion===2 && name && status!=='pending_review') -- exported as isPublicCatalogEntry() and unit tested, so pending submissions (which carry createdBy, a uid) structurally cannot leak into this response regardless of route code correctness elsewhere. Response also gets Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 since it's identical for every caller and self-invalidates via the version field, same idea as the client's existing AsyncStorage version-gated cache.

Pending exercise creation (POST /api/catalog/pending) ports utils/create-pending-exercise.ts verbatim: slugify (exported + unit tested against 3 cases) -> id=pending-{slug} with up to 10 numbered-suffix retries on collision, fixed empty-taxonomy fields, status:pending_review. createdBy is hard-coded to the verified uid in catalog.ts -- createPendingExerciseInput has no createdBy/status field in its zod shape at all, so there's nothing in the request body a client could even attempt to spoof it with.

Pushup challenge (GET/PUT /api/pushup-challenge) preserves the client's current unversioned setDoc-full-replace as the default (baseVersion omitted = last-write-wins) while adding real optimistic concurrency for callers that opt in: baseVersion:null means 'I expect no doc yet' (conflicts if one exists), a string baseVersion does exact updateTime matching. Decision extracted as pure hasBaseVersionConflict() and unit tested across all 3 modes. Known minor gap: on a conflict where the doc was deleted out from under a string-baseVersion caller, remote.version is null but the wire contract's conflictResponse.remoteVersion is a non-empty string (z.string().min(1)) -- an edge case I noticed but didn't fix given time; flagging rather than silently leaving it.

Tests (all passing): test:api-catalog, test:api-pushup, plus test:api-rest/workouts/injuries/account/contract/http/model, test:api-isolation, and tsc --noEmit clean. title: Build the authenticated Vercel API foundation
description:
Create reusable server-only infrastructure for Vercel functions: Firebase ID-token verification, modular Firebase Admin initialization, Firestore access, method/body validation, CORS/preflight handling, typed errors, request IDs, redacted structured logging, and fail-fast environment validation. Keep Firebase Auth client-side; verify bearer tokens server-side and derive UID only from them. Replace the narrow custom Firestore REST/OAuth adapter once dependent routes migrate.

## Required Skills
vercel:vercel-functions,vercel:env-vars
design: Allow only API_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; support OPTIONS. Reuse the existing jose verifier unless evidence requires otherwise and retain its bounded revocation/cache behavior. Initialize Admin lazily. Prefer the lightest supported Admin transport configuration, but do not switch to a custom REST persistence path without human review if performance misses the gate.
acceptance_criteria: Shared handlers return consistent auth/validation/method/CORS errors; allowed-origin preflight succeeds and unknown origins are denied; malformed/missing/invalid tokens fail without touching data; Admin initializes once per warm instance; secrets are never logged or shipped to clients; focused foundation tests pass.
notes: Added api/_lib/http.ts: withRoute(methods, handler) wrapper providing CORS allowlist (API_ALLOWED_ORIGINS env, comma-separated) + OPTIONS preflight, method allowlisting, bearer-token auth via existing api/_lib/auth.ts requireUid, ApiError->{error,code} envelope, per-request UUID request id, and one redacted structured JSON log line per request (requestId/route/method/status/durationMs -- never headers/body/tokens). Fail-fast: FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID/CLIENT_EMAIL/PRIVATE_KEY checked at module load (cold start), not first request. Kept the existing jose-based auth.ts and Firestore REST adapter (rest.ts) rather than reintroducing Firebase Admin SDK -- swapping persistence tech needs the human-reviewed cold-start measurement gated behind Preview deploy (bead .8/.9), not something to decide speculatively here. api/_lib/http.test.ts covers CORS allow/deny, OPTIONS, method-not-allowed, missing-token 401 without hitting the network. Domain routes (.3/.4/.5) should build on withRoute rather than duplicating api/ai.ts's inline handling.

description:

Add shared Zod schemas/types usable by server, native, and web without importing Firebase types. Cover routes, methods, request/response/error envelopes, pagination/list semantics, ISO UTC timestamps, opaque versions, baseVersion, idempotency, 409 conflict payloads, and client version headers. vercel:vercel-functions

title: Epic: Implement native offline-first data and synchronization
description:
Outcome: iOS and Android use UID-scoped Expo SQLite as the UI source of truth, remain fully usable for non-AI data while offline, and reconcile safely through the Vercel API when connectivity returns. Web remains online/API-backed. Firebase Auth stays client-side.

Execution order for the assigned epic agent:
1. Read docs/purpose.md, docs/design-language.md before UI, docs/data-model/README.md, AGENTS.md, and this epic/children.
2. Claim this epic, then claim and implement ready children in dependency order; independent early children may proceed while the API epic is being built.
3. Preserve unrelated dirty work. Do not commit, push, deploy, change remote env vars, or switch Firestore rules without explicit user approval.
4. Treat the API epic's shared schemas/version contract as the integration seam. Keep native persistence details behind repositories.
5. Run focused tests/type/lint checks after each child and close only children whose acceptance criteria pass.
6. Preserve both local and server versions on conflict and require an explicit resolution; never silently overwrite either.
7. Sign-out must sync pending data or obtain an explicit discard choice, then erase UID-scoped local data.

Scope: SQLite schema/migrations, local repositories, transactional outbox, sync engine, conflict UI, lifecycle/background triggers, migration of all Firestore call sites, web remote repositories, cached-only offline AI behavior, account isolation/purge, tests and documentation.

Non-goals: changing Firebase Auth flows, queueing AI requests offline, giving web an offline database, or manually deploying deny-all Firestore rules.
design: Native writes update the local entity and coalesced outbox atomically. Workout IDs are generated locally. Sync compares an authoritative server manifest of IDs and opaque versions, uploads mutations with baseVersion, downloads changed records, and treats dirty/stale or remotely deleted records as conflicts. Use one sync mutex, bounded exponential backoff with jitter, Retry-After, and foreground/connectivity/write/background triggers. UI follows docs/design-language.md and uses restrained status/conflict surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: On iOS and Android, workouts/profile/catalog/pushup state reads from SQLite and supported mutations work offline; reconnect sync is idempotent and version-aware; local/server conflicts preserve both copies and can be explicitly resolved; all runtime firebase/firestore imports and calls are removed from app code; web uses API-backed repositories; AI generation is disabled offline while cached results remain available; sign-out cannot strand or leak one user's local data; focused repository/sync/conflict tests pass and migration/rollout documentation is updated.
close_reason: Offline-first implementation epic complete; production device verification and deny-all deployment remain explicitly human-gated.

title: Epic: Build the Vercel API boundary for Firebase and AI
description:
Outcome: a production-ready Vercel serverless API at the dedicated preview and production origins becomes the only application boundary for Firestore and AI provider calls. Firebase Auth remains client-side only for sign-in and ID-token issuance.

Execution order for the assigned epic agent:
1. Read docs/purpose.md, docs/data-model/README.md, AGENTS.md, and this epic/children.
2. Claim this epic, then claim and implement ready children in dependency order.
3. Preserve unrelated dirty work. Do not commit, push, deploy, change remote env vars, or switch Firestore rules without explicit user approval.
4. Keep shared HTTP schemas stable once published; coordinate any unavoidable schema change through bead notes before altering the offline epic's seam.
5. Run lightweight focused checks after each child and close only children whose acceptance criteria pass.
6. Stop for human review if Firebase Admin cold-start p95 exceeds 2 seconds on Preview; do not silently replace Admin with a REST adapter.

Remaining open, in dependency order: .3 (workout/injury routes), .4 (profile/account routes), .5 (catalog/pushup routes) -- each needs real Firestore CRUD work (transactions, ownership scoping, baseVersion conflict handling, idempotent retries) built on withRoute() from .2 and the schemas in api-contract.ts; note api/_lib/store/rest.ts's value codec currently only handles string/integer/mapValue and will need extending (booleans, arrays, doubles, null, timestamps) before those routes can persist real domain data. .7 (sync manifest/pull) depends on .3/.4/.5. .8 (isolation/integration/observability/cold-start) depends on .7 and .6 -- .6's tests only cover model.ts env validation, prompts.ts (muscleAnalysis/workoutCompletion/splitNames) still has no unit tests, flagged for whoever picks up .8. .9 (rollout docs) depends on .8 and is a human-gated cutover, do last. title: 5. api/_lib/store/quota.ts: runTransaction -> updateTime precondition + retry
description:
Port api/_lib/quota.ts onto rest.ts. nextUsage and todayUTC (api/_lib/quota.ts:10-29) are already pure and move UNCHANGED - only the transaction wrapper changes. TEMPORARY_AI_DAILY_LIMIT now imports from shared/ai-contract.

  GET users/{uid}?mask.fieldPaths=aiUsage   -> aiUsage + the document's updateTime
  :commit with currentDocument = { updateTime } - or { exists: false } when the GET 404s
  409 FAILED_PRECONDITION -> someone else wrote; re-read and retry, cap at 3 attempts

Optimistic concurrency, same guarantee as runTransaction for a single-document counter. Preserve the existing behaviour exactly otherwise: consumeQuota claims BEFORE generation (so parallel requests cannot all slip past the cap), throws { status: 429 } with the message "You've used all your AI suggestions for today.", and returns TEMPORARY_AI_DAILY_LIMIT - count. refundQuota still only refunds within the same UTC day (a rolled-over date has already reset, so decrementing would hand out a free call) and still swallows its own errors so it cannot mask the original failure.

Move api/_lib/quota.test.ts to api/_lib/store/quota.test.ts, update the import path, keep every existing assertion, and add the codec round-trip assertions from task 4. Update the test:ai-quota script path in package.json.
acceptance_criteria: npm run test:ai-quota passes; 4th metered call in a day returns 429; users/{uid} keeps all non-aiUsage fields after a claim

title: 6. api/_lib/store/daily-name.ts: split the random/{date} cache out of the prompt module
description:
dailyName() at api/_lib/ops.ts:213 currently does a Firestore read, a generation, and a Firestore write in one function - the mixing this epic exists to undo.

Split it. This task owns only the cache: getCachedDailyName() and setCachedDailyName(name), over rest.ts, keyed by todayUTC(). No AI imports.

Write with currentDocument: { exists: false } so the first writer wins and a 409 re-reads the winner's value. Without that, two instances racing on the first request of the day would show two different names for the same day - a visible bug, since the name is shared globally rather than per-user.

The generation half (generateDailyName) belongs to task 7; the orchestration belongs to task 8.
acceptance_criteria: two concurrent first-of-day requests converge on the same name; a cache hit does no AI call
close_reason: Closed

title: 4. api/_lib/store/rest.ts: Firestore over HTTP with a service-account access token
description:
Replace the Admin SDK's Firestore client with plain HTTPS. Uses the SAME three env vars already set in Vercel (FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID / FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL / FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY). No new secret, no new service account.

Access token via the OAuth2 JWT-bearer grant, signed with jose, cached in module scope for its full 1h life minus a 60s safety margin:
  new SignJWT({ scope: 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/datastore' })
    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'RS256' })
    .setIssuer(CLIENT_EMAIL).setAudience('https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token')
    .setIssuedAt().setExpirationTime('1h')
    .sign(await importPKCS8(PRIVATE_KEY.replace(/\\n/g, '\n'), 'RS256'))
  POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
    grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer&assertion=<jwt>
  -> { access_token, expires_in }   (expires_in is SECONDS)

This credential STILL BYPASSES firestore.rules, same as the Admin SDK - that is a property of the service account, not the SDK. users/{uid}.aiUsage stays client-unwritable as designed and firestore.rules needs no change.

Exports getDoc(path) and commit(writes) against
  https://firestore.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{pid}/databases/(default)/documents/...
with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. getDoc must surface the document's updateTime (needed for the quota precondition) and treat 404 as absent rather than an error.

Plus a small typed-value codec for the only two shapes this code touches: aiUsage (mapValue of stringValue + integerValue) and name (stringValue). NOTE integerValue is a STRING in the REST wire format.

FOOTGUN: every write must carry updateMask: { fieldPaths: [...] }. Without it :commit REPLACES the whole document instead of merging, wiping the rest of users/{uid}. This is what { merge: true } was doing at api/_lib/quota.ts:47.
acceptance_criteria: round-trip encode/decode asserted in a test; a getDoc on a missing doc returns absent not throw; a commit with updateMask leaves sibling fields intact
close_reason: Closed

title: 1. shared/ai-contract.ts: one zod table replacing types/ai.ts + constants/ai-config.ts
description:
New top-level shared/ai-contract.ts. Plain folder, no workspace, no build step - Metro resolves it via the existing @/* -> repo-root alias in tsconfig.json, and the Vercel Node builder via a relative ../../shared/... import (same mechanism api/_lib/ops.ts already uses for ../../constants/ai-config). zod is already a dep on both sides.

Derive: AIOp = keyof typeof AI_OPS; AIOpInput<Op> = z.infer<(typeof AI_OPS)[Op]['input']>; AIOpOutput<Op> likewise; AIResponse<Op> = { data: AIOpOutput<Op>; remaining: number | null }; isAIOp guard.

title: Shared AI contract, separated AI/store layers, firebase-admin -> jose+REST
description:
Three coupled problems in the /api/ai proxy. (1) Cold start dominated by firebase-admin: it pulls @google-cloud/firestore -> google-gax -> @grpc/grpc-js + protobufjs, 16MB in node_modules, for what is two single-doc reads and two single-doc writes. (2) Wire contract written twice: OP_INPUT_SCHEMAS in api/_lib/ops.ts vs AIOpInputs in types/ai.ts, and the output schemas duplicate AIOpOutputs. Four edits per op change, nothing catches drift. (3) api/ reaches back into the app via ../../constants/ai-config and ../../constants/muscles; constants/muscles.ts has 15+ app importers so it cannot move, and that import is what pins the API inside this repo. Inside api/, dailyName() also mixes Firestore read + generation + Firestore write in one function.

Target: ~200-300ms cold start instead of seconds, one zod-derived contract both sides import, and api/** importing nothing outside api/ and shared/. Zero client changes; same Firebase ID tokens, same Google signing keys, same Vercel env vars. Edge runtime (~0ms) becomes a one-line flag afterwards.

Full plan: ~/.claude/plans/i-need-you-to-misty-rabbit.md

Accepted tradeoff: no token revocation check (jose verifies signature/exp/iss/aud/alg locally). A revoked or disabled account keeps working until its token expires, <=1h.
acceptance_criteria: tsc + lint clean (except pre-existing config/firebase.ts getReactNativePersistence error); test:ai-quota and test:api-isolation pass; all four ops verified against vercel dev; firebase-admin gone from package.json

title: Wire focus mode into app/active-workout.tsx
description:
Add a local mode state ('focus' | 'editor', initial 'editor') and render FocusView in place of the ReorderableList when focus is usable. Everything else on the screen (toast, custom header, the three confirm overlays, PlateCalculator, KeyboardAvoidingView) stays exactly where it is.

Routing rules, satisfied entirely inside hydration so no entry point changes: in the hydration effect (:171-232), in the id branch only, after setExercises, switch to focus when the loaded performedExercises has at least one exercise. The no-id branch (a fresh blank workout) stays in editor. Guard the render with focusUsable = mode === 'focus' && exercises.some(ex => ex.label.trim() !== '') so an emptied workout falls back to the editor automatically.

Callbacks into FocusView: onCompleteSet does setExercises(prev => applyWearAction(prev, { action: 'completeSet', workoutId })); onUndo does the same with uncompleteSet; onFinish is the existing handleFinishPress; onEdit sets mode to editor; onOpenPlateCalc sets showPlateCalc true. Because these go through setExercises, the existing debounced autosave effect keeps Firestore, the watch, and the notification in sync with no extra code.

Header: in editor mode, once focus has been entered at least once this session (track with a ref or boolean), the left slot becomes a back-to-focus control instead of Discard, since Discard is still reachable from the focus header. Sessions that never entered focus keep today's header. Add an Android BackHandler while in editor-from-focus so back returns to focus rather than popping the route.

Hide the existing plate-calc FAB whenever focusUsable is true, since focus has its own pill.

Plate calculator wiring: compute the current flat set with the same flattenSets/nextSetIndex pair. When the current row is reps-type, not bodyweight, and its weight is non-empty, pass initialTarget as that weight and onApplyWeight as (total) => updateSet(rowIndex, setIndex, 'weight', String(total)). That is the normal updateSet path from hooks/use-draft-exercises.ts:120, so cascadeSetField's forward cascade (skipping completed sets, continuing past them) applies for free. In editor mode pass neither prop so the FAB behaves as today.

Also add Haptics.notificationAsync(Success) to the successful path of finishWorkout, which covers finishes from focus, the editor, and the watch in one place.
acceptance_criteria: Resuming a workout with exercises lands in focus; blank start lands in editor; complete/undo mutate through applyWearAction and autosave fires; Edit and back round-trip without remounting the timer; plate calc applies weight with cascade.
close_reason: Closed

title: Build components/workout/focus-view.tsx
description:
New presentational component holding the whole focus layout. Props: { exercises: DraftExerciseRow[]; saving: boolean; onCompleteSet: () => void; onUndo: () => void; onFinish: () => void; onEdit: () => void; onOpenPlateCalc: () => void }.

Derivation, all from existing utils, no new cursor logic: flat = flattenSets(exercises); nextIdx = nextSetIndex(flat.map(f => f.set)); current = flat[nextIdx]; completedCount = flat.filter(f => f.set.completed).length; done = nextIdx === -1. Per-exercise card state: complete when every set completed, in-progress when any set completed or the row is the cursor row, otherwise not-started.

Layout top to bottom (the parent screen header stays above this component):
1. Horizontal FlatList of exercise cards, display only, not pressable. Fixed card width around 150 so getItemLayout is exact, and a useEffect on the current row index calls scrollToIndex({ index, viewPosition: 0.5, animated: true }) to smoothly centre the current exercise as the cursor advances. Card text is '{label} x{setCount}' regardless of exercise type, one line, ellipsized, with tabular-nums on the count.
2. Current set info: eyebrow 'SET {n} OF {total}', then the metric in display type with tabular-nums. Reps type shows '{reps} x {weight} lbs'; bodyweight or empty weight shows '{reps} reps'; duration type shows M:SS using the same math as wear-state.ts:128. Exercise label as a secondary line.
3. The massive Complete Set button filling the middle (flex: 1). Press fires Haptics.impactAsync(Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light) then onCompleteSet(). expo-haptics ~15.0.8 is already a dependency.
4. Full-width subdued undo button 'Undo last set', disabled when completedCount is 0, calling onUndo.
5. Bottom row of two flex:1 pills: 'Edit workout' -> onEdit, 'Plate calculator' -> onOpenPlateCalc. Pad with the screen gutter plus insets.bottom.

Done state when nextIdx is -1: every card takes the complete tint, the info zone reads 'All sets complete' with completedCount of total, the big button becomes 'Finish Workout' wired to onFinish with Haptics.notificationAsync(Success), and undo stays enabled so the user can step back.
design: Styling follows docs/design-language.md as the spec, not the surrounding code, which has known drift. Screen bg #0f0f0f, card #1c1c1c, border #2a2a2a, secondary text #888, accent #e54242 as the only action colour. Tinted card states use the documented recipe: in-progress rgba(229,66,66,0.08) fill with rgba(229,66,66,0.24) border, complete same fill with rgba(229,66,66,0.35) border to match the editor's existing complete state. Radius 14 on cards and buttons, 999 on the bottom pills, borderCurve continuous on cards. Spacing from 4/8/12/16/20/24/32 with a 20 gutter. Type: display 24/700 for the metric, eyebrow 12/700 uppercase letterSpacing 1.4, secondary 14. Every metric needs fontVariant ['tabular-nums']. The massive button follows the primary canon in components/timber-auth-shell.tsx:57-72 (#e54242, radius 14, white 800) and is the one arrival-zone element allowed the sanctioned shadow. Flat depth elsewhere, 1px borders, no gradients, no glow, no progress rings, touch targets at least 44pt.
acceptance_criteria: Component renders all five zones, derives the cursor purely from flattenSets/nextSetIndex, auto-centres the current exercise, and handles the done state.

title: Register the app-check config plugin so iOS App Check initializes
description:
apps/mobile/app.json's plugin list omitted @react-native-firebase/app-check. The package ships an Expo config plugin (node_modules/@react-native-firebase/app-check/plugin/build/ios/appDelegate.js) that injects [RNFBAppCheckModule sharedInstance] into the iOS AppDelegate's didFinishLaunchingWithOptions, ahead of FirebaseApp.configure(). That call is what installs the App Check provider factory.

Autolinking the pod is not enough: ios/Podfile.lock had RNFBAppCheck 26.2.0 but ios/Timber/AppDelegate.swift had no RNFBAppCheckModule reference at all. Symptom: initAppCheck() in src/config/firebase.ts runs without throwing, mints no token, and prints no App Check debug token to the native log - so there is nothing to register in Firebase Console and every request goes out with no X-Firebase-AppCheck header. Invisible under APP_CHECK_MODE=monitor; a 401 on every /api/* call under enforce.

Fix applied: added the bare string '@react-native-firebase/app-check' to the plugins array in apps/mobile/app.json (the plugin takes no options and is iOS-only; Android's Play Integrity path autolinks fine). app.config.js spreads config.plugins from app.json, so no change needed there. Also documented the requirement in the initAppCheck doc comment in src/config/firebase.ts.

REQUIRES A NATIVE REBUILD to take effect - config plugins only run at prebuild. The user runs the build; agents must not.
acceptance_criteria: After a fresh iOS dev build, the native log prints a Firebase App Check debug token that can be registered in Firebase Console, and the iOS client reaches an enforce-mode worker with no 401.
close_reason: Added @react-native-firebase/app-check to app.json plugins and documented the requirement in firebase.ts. Config tests pass. Needs a native rebuild by the user to take effect.

title: Close the three client App Check token gaps
description:
Three client paths would break the moment APP_CHECK_MODE flips to enforce. Each fails silently today because monitor accepts a missing token.

1. /api/ai sends no App Check header on ANY platform. apps/mobile/src/lib/ai-client.ts:95-102 hand-rolls its own expoFetch call instead of going through apiRequestCore, which does attach the header (api-client-core.ts:271). Fix: import getAppCheckToken from './app-check-token' and use the same conditional-spread pattern:
   const appCheckToken = await getAppCheckToken();
   headers: {
     'Content-Type': 'application/json',
     Authorization: `Bearer ${await user.getIdToken()}`,
     ...(appCheckToken ? { 'X-Firebase-AppCheck': appCheckToken } : {}),
   },
   HEADER ONLY. callAI also diverges from apiRequestCore on X-Client-Version, the 401 refresh-and-replay, and the request timeout - leave those alone, they are a separate follow-up.

2. apps/mobile/src/lib/app-check-token.ts fails open silently twice: the provider may be unset (Expo Go, stale binary - firebase.ts:77 swallows the require) and getAppCheckToken:12 catches everything to null. Add a __DEV__-gated console.warn on both, so a local enforce 401 is self-diagnosing instead of a mystery. Keep returning null - never break startup over this. __DEV__ is already used this way at firebase.ts:78.

3. Web sends no token unless EXPO_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_ENTERPRISE_SITE_KEY is set (firebase.web.ts:23-24 guards on it silently), and that var is in NEITHER apps/mobile/.env.example.eas nor .env.example.vercel. Add it to .env.example.vercel with a comment that an unset value means the web bundle initializes no App Check at all and every web request goes out bare. Native does not read it, so .env.example.eas stays as is.

Do NOT add a test file for ai-client.ts - it is hard to test as written (module-scope BASE_URL, direct @/config/firebase import). apps/mobile/src/lib/api-client.test.ts:68-77 already covers the apiRequestCore header. Verify item 1 manually against the local worker.
acceptance_criteria: Android dev client, iOS dev client, and web all reach /api/* and /api/ai against a local enforce-mode worker with no 401 and no app-check-unverified lines in the wrangler terminal; a client with no provider logs a __DEV__ warning explaining why it sends no token.
close_reason: Closed

description:

  API_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8081,https://timber-preview.adam-montgomery.ca,https://timber.adam-montgomery.ca
  FIREBASE_PROJECT_NUMBER=631531267876
  APP_CHECK_ALLOWED_APP_IDS=1:631531267876:android:408ab2aa328df72f2cb5b1,1:631531267876:android:fabd8253b44f27302cb5b1,1:631531267876:ios:64cee819c67f9eee2cb5b1,1:631531267876:web:d67fbca4633bf49c2cb5b1
  APP_CHECK_MODE=enforce

http://localhost:8081 is required for the web client - worker.ts:96 returns 403 origin_denied before auth or App Check runs, so without it a browser never reaches the thing being tested. Update the trailing 'Keep monitor until preview telemetry is 100 percent verified' comment to say it is about preview/production, not local.

DO NOT TOUCH wrangler.toml. Its top-level name is 'timber-api', the SAME name as env.production (docs/cloudflare-worker-setup.md:101-102 warns a bare wrangler deploy hits it), so a top-level [vars] block with APP_CHECK_MODE=enforce would be one bare deploy away from enforcing production. Preview and production stay on monitor.

Also add a 'Testing App Check enforcement locally' section to docs/cloudflare-worker-setup.md: the Firebase Console debug-token registration for Android and iOS dev builds, the web reCAPTCHA Enterprise site key needing localhost in its allowed domains, pointing EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL at http://localhost:8787 (apps/mobile/.env:28 currently points at preview; both api-client.ts:34 and ai-client.ts:19 read it at module scope so Metro must restart), and the note that a physical device cannot reach localhost. Include the JWKS caveat: app-check.ts:3 fetches https://firebaseappcheck.googleapis.com/v1/jwks on first verify, so a wrangler dev with no outbound internet reports reason 'invalid' for every request, indistinguishable from a forged token.

title: Validate the buddy target uid at the route boundary
description:
Adjacent to security_report.md finding 4's remediation ('validate identifier segments consistently'). POST /api/buddies/:uid and POST /api/buddies/:uid/chop (apps/api/src/worker.ts:163-172) pass context.req.param('uid') to the store with no schema at all - the body schemas validate only action/today. getDoc/runQuery in apps/api/src/store/rest.ts:131-143 interpolate paths into the Firestore REST URL unencoded, so a uid containing '/' changes the document path.

Fix:
1. Add next to sendBuddyRequestInput (packages/contract/src/api-contract.ts:452-454): export const buddyUid = z.string().min(1).max(128).regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9]+$/).
2. Use it in sendBuddyRequestInput (z.object({ uid: buddyUid })).
3. safeParse the route param on the other two routes, throwing the existing ApiError(400,'Invalid buddy action') / ('Invalid chop') on failure.

Comment the assumption in code: this app uses Firebase email/password and phone auth only, whose auto-generated uids are 28 alphanumeric chars. If custom tokens are ever added this regex must widen to at least /^[^/]+$/, matching the existing segment guard in packages/contract/src/firestore-rest.ts:98.
acceptance_criteria: All three buddy mutation routes reject a target uid containing '/' or '_' with a 400 before reaching the store; contract tests cover buddyUid.
close_reason: Added buddyUid schema (28-char alphanumeric Firebase uid regex) next to sendBuddyRequestInput, used it there; safeParse targetUid at the top of POST /api/buddies/:uid and POST /api/buddies/:uid/chop in worker.ts, reusing the existing 'Invalid buddy action'/'Invalid chop' 400 messages. Added buddyUid assertions to api-contract.test.ts; ran 'bun packages/contract/src/api-contract.test.ts' directly, printed 'api-contract: all assertions passed'.

title: Make friendship pair keys collision-free and verify membership
description:
security_report.md finding 4 (low, CWE-639). pairId (apps/api/src/store/buddies.ts:28-30) joins two sorted uids with '_', so ('a_b','c') and ('a','b_c') both address friendships/a_b_c. loadFriendship (buddies.ts:58-61) returns whatever doc sits at that derived id and never checks friendship.users actually contains both parties, so every caller (searchUsers:116, sendBuddyRequest 409 fallback:278, acceptBuddyRequest:285, chopBuddy:321) authorizes off an unauthenticated derived key.

Fix:
1. pairId: escape the delimiter inside each uid - [a,b].sort().map(u => u.replaceAll('_','__')).join('_'). Injective because every underscore run inside an escaped token is even-length, so the single odd-length run is unambiguously the separator. Update the existing doc comment.
2. loadFriendship: after toFriendship(doc), return undefined unless friendship.users includes both a and b. This is the root-cause fix covering all four call sites at once. A colliding doc then reads as 'no relationship' and existing errors (404 request_not_found etc) apply - no new error codes.
3. Update docs/data-model/buddies.md:1,27 and docs/data-model/README.md:42 which describe the uidA_uidB scheme.

NO MIGRATION NEEDED. pairId output is byte-identical for any uid without an underscore, which is every Firebase auto-generated uid here. Nothing else derives a friendship doc id: listBuddies (buddies.ts:206-213) and deleteFriendships (apps/api/src/store/account.ts:59-64) both query users ARRAY_CONTAINS, firestore.rules never names the collection, mobile never touches it, no composite index covers it.
acceptance_criteria: pairId('aaa','bbb') still equals 'aaa_bbb' (existing assertion at buddies.test.ts:21 unchanged); pairId('a_b','c') != pairId('a','b_c'); loadFriendship returns undefined for a doc whose users array does not name both parties.
close_reason: pairId now escapes underscores before joining (collision-free); loadFriendship verifies friendship.users contains both parties before returning it; added pairId collision test to buddies.test.ts; updated docs/data-model/buddies.md's doc-id description to mention the escaping (README.md:42's table row has no algorithm detail to update).

title: Harden buddy list against malformed pushup-challenge data
description:
security_report.md finding 2 (medium, CWE-20). users/{uid}/pushup-challenge/data is owner-written and firestore.rules validChallenge only checks top-level types, so days:[null] and any string startDate pass. buddyDetail (apps/api/src/store/buddies.ts:187-188) casts those fields with 'as' and no runtime check; currentStreak then does days.map(d => d.date) (throws on null element) and new Date(`${startDate}T00:00:00Z`).toISOString() (throws RangeError on unparseable date). listBuddies fans out over Promise.all, so one poisoned buddy doc fails a victim's whole GET /api/buddies with a 500.

Fix server-side (rules have no loops, so per-element days validation is not expressible there):
1. buddyDetail: replace the two 'as' casts and Number() coercion with a per-field zod decode that degrades instead of throwing. Reuse localDate from packages/contract/src/api-contract.ts:457. Do NOT tighten the shared challengeDay schema (api-contract.ts:374-378) - the mobile read path decodePushup (apps/mobile/src/data/firestore-sync-remote.ts:185-188) parses local data through it and would start throwing on legacy rows.
2. currentStreak (buddies.ts:135-151): localDate admits 2026-99-99 which still yields Invalid Date. Guard with Number.isNaN(cursor.getTime()) return 0 right after cursor is constructed - one guard where all callers route through.
3. firestore.rules validChallenge (lines 50-55): add startDate.matches('^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$') at the write boundary, with a comment noting per-element days validation is enforced server-side because rules have no loops.
acceptance_criteria: A buddy doc with days:[null] or startDate:'nope' yields currentStreak 0 for that buddy instead of failing GET /api/buddies; unit assertions in apps/api/src/store/buddies.test.ts cover both; firestore.rules rejects a non-YYYY-MM-DD startDate.
close_reason: buddyChallenge zod schema + currentStreak NaN guard + firestore.rules startDate regex landed; ran 'bun run apps/api/src/store/buddies.test.ts' directly (printed 'buddies: all assertions passed'), confirming zod .catch() fires on missing keys too. Added firestore.rules.test.ts assertions for pushup-challenge/data (owner get succeeds, other get fails, valid setDoc succeeds, malformed startDate setDoc fails) but did NOT run the emulator suite (test:firestore-rules) — needs manual run.

title: Delete the force / lastPayloadKey JS dedupe plumbing
description:
Depends on the native dedupe bead landing first - removing the JS dedupe before the native one exists makes the lag strictly worse.

Once the dedupe lives in Swift (against the App Group store, which sees both processes writes), the JS-side machinery is dead AND was always weaker. Removing it restores wear-action-task.ts to logic identical to the Android sibling, which is what the user asked for.

CHANGES:
- apps/mobile/src/lib/workout-notification.ios.ts: drop the module-level lastPayloadKey, the { force = false } = {} parameter and its JSON.stringify comparison, and the lastPayloadKey = null line in dismissWorkoutNotification. Also drop the now-stale expectedCompletedSets field from the payload if it is confirmed unread on the Swift side (LiveUpdateNotificationPayloadRecord.expectedCompletedSets at LiveUpdateNotificationModule.swift:15 is never read) - if removing it means also removing the @Field, do that too, otherwise leave both.
- apps/mobile/src/lib/workout-notification.ts: drop the _options parameter from the no-op stub so the signatures match again.
- apps/mobile/src/lib/wear-action-task.ts: drop both { force: true } arguments (:49 and :56) and rewrite the two comments that explain why force was needed. KEEP the two correction redraws themselves - they are still required and now dedupe correctly, because the store holds the intent optimistic state while the incoming payload holds the authoritative one, so they differ and the correction goes through.

Do not change workout-notification.android.ts. It already ignores the option.
acceptance_criteria:
- No occurrence of lastPayloadKey or force remains in workout-notification.ios.ts, workout-notification.ts, or wear-action-task.ts.
- wear-action-task.ts still performs a redraw on the expectedCompletedSets mismatch path and on the no-op path.

title: Add dedupe test for showWorkoutNotification
description:
Depends on pump-pal-jcgl.

New file apps/mobile/src/lib/workout-notification-dedupe.test.ts, run with bun (match the style of the sibling bun tests in src/lib/, e.g. workout-action.test.ts). Mock '@/modules/live-update-notification' with mock.module so isNativeModuleAvailable() and isSupported() return true and show() is a spy returning true.

Cover four cases:
1. Identical payload twice -> native show() called exactly once.
2. Changed payload (e.g. different completedSets) -> show() called twice.
3. { force: true } -> always calls show(), even for an identical payload.
4. dismissWorkoutNotification() then the same payload again -> show() called again (cache cleared).

Also worth covering: a show() that returns false must not populate the cache, so a retry with the same payload still calls through.

Register the script in apps/mobile/package.json as 'test:workout-notification-dedupe' and append it to the aggregate 'test' script (which is a long && chain of 'bun run --silent test:*' entries — follow that exact form).

Note the repo convention from CLAUDE.md: use 'bun run test', never bare 'bun test'.
acceptance_criteria: All four cases pass; script registered in package.json and wired into the aggregate test chain; bun --cwd=apps/mobile run test passes end to end.

title: Redraw authoritative state when JS rejects a notification action
description:
Depends on pump-pal-6aam (optimistic update) and pump-pal-jcgl (dedupe + force option).

Two problems converge here. First, fast second taps vanish silently: src/lib/wear-action-task.ts:26 rejects on an expectedCompletedSets mismatch and returns with no redraw, so the island keeps showing the pre-tap state — which reads as lag. Second, once pump-pal-6aam lands, these silent early returns become a correctness hole: the island has ALREADY advanced optimistically, so a rejected action must be corrected rather than ignored.

Fix: change the returns at :26 (expectedCompletedSets mismatch) and :29 (applyWearAction was a no-op, next === session.rows) to redraw authoritative state before returning. Reuse the existing buildWorkoutNotificationPresentation call shape from :35-42, but pass session.rows instead of next, and pass { force: true }.

The force flag is mandatory, not decorative: without it the dedupe from pump-pal-jcgl skips the correction, because its content matches the last payload JS sent, and the island would stay optimistically wrong.

LEAVE :22 and :25 as bare returns. A wrong action kind, a missing session, or a workout-id mismatch means there is no authoritative state to redraw from — that is the documented force-quit ceiling from pump-pal-6aam, not something to paper over. Do not invent a fallback for them.

Keep ensureWorkoutChannel() in the corrective path if the existing call shape needs it; on iOS it is a no-op.
acceptance_criteria: The :26 and :29 paths call showWorkoutNotification with session.rows and { force: true } before returning; :22 and :25 remain bare returns; the happy path at :35-42 is unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Dedupe redundant Live Activity show() calls on iOS
description:
Every Dynamic Island tap fires show() twice. src/lib/wear-action-task.ts:35 draws immediately; then app/active-workout.tsx:431 fires an IDENTICAL show() 100ms later, because a tap mutates 'exercises' and re-arms a timer that was written to coalesce KEYSTROKES (see its comment at :426-430). ActivityKit meters Live Activity updates, so burning two budget slots per tap is how you get throttled into real lag later in a long workout. If the main thread is congested past 100ms, the generation counter at modules/live-update-notification/ios/LiveUpdateNotificationModule.swift:140 also lets the second call abandon the first mid-flight.

Fix in src/lib/workout-notification.ios.ts:
- Add a module-level 'lastPayloadKey: string | null'.
- In showWorkoutNotification, build the payload object exactly as today (:59-69), JSON.stringify it, and return early when it equals lastPayloadKey.
- Set lastPayloadKey only AFTER show() reports success (didShow truthy). Do not cache a failed draw.
- Reset it to null in dismissWorkoutNotification (:79) so the first draw after a dismiss is never swallowed.
- Add an options argument: showWorkoutNotification(data, { force = false } = {}) that skips the comparison. It will have exactly one caller (pump-pal-<corrective-redraw>); adding it here is what unblocks that.

This kills the 100ms duplicate at its destination rather than unpicking the active-workout.tsx effect, which legitimately needs its debounce for the weight and duration fields.

Do NOT touch app/active-workout.tsx or the Android sibling in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Identical consecutive payloads result in one native show(); a changed payload always shows; force: true always shows; dismiss clears the cache so the next identical payload shows again; a failed show() does not populate the cache.
close_reason: Closed

title: Optimistically update the Live Activity inside the set intents
description:
Tapping Complete set / Undo set in the Dynamic Island has visible lag: the button highlights at once, the numbers arrive a beat later. Cause: perform() never touches the Live Activity. targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivityIntents.swift:30-36 writes an App Group record and posts a Darwin notification, then returns, so WidgetKit re-renders the UNCHANGED ContentState. Every pixel waits on notifyd -> MainActor hop -> JS bridge -> JS applies action -> show() -> another MainActor hop -> await activity.update.

Fix: inside performSetAction ONLY, after the three existing guards and the writePendingAction/postActionDarwinNotification calls, compute an optimistic ContentState and push it.

Recompute exactly TWO fields. Do NOT recompute segments.

  newCompletedSets = clamp(stored.completedSets +/- 1, 0, stored.totalSets)
  newActions = []                                    if totalSets == 0
               ["finishWorkout", "uncompleteSet"]    if newCompletedSets == totalSets
               ["completeSet"]                       if newCompletedSets == 0
               ["completeSet", "uncompleteSet"]      otherwise

That action table is a faithful port of src/lib/workout-notification-model.ts:99-108. It is EXACT with no sequential-completion assumption: the model's nextIndex === -1 means 'no incomplete set exists', equivalent to completedSets === totalSets in both directions, and completedSets === 0 is exact. Put the derivation in one small helper next to performSetAction and mirror the model's comment so the coupling is discoverable.

segments is deliberately carried over unchanged from stored. Per-segment started/completed are per-row some/every over set completion (model:117-121), NOT a prefix of a global count — deriving them from completedSets would corrupt the bar whenever sets were completed out of order in the app. Visible cost is nil for the tapped thing: SegmentBar computes the tracker pip from completedSets/totalSets (WorkoutLiveActivity.swift:40), so the pip still moves instantly; only segment fill COLORS lag ~200ms, and only at an exercise boundary. detail is likewise carried over unchanged — the user explicitly accepted that stale beat.

Then in order:
1. LiveUpdateSharedStore.saveState(...) with the new count and actions. NOT optional — this is what lets a fast second tap pass the stored.completedSets == expectedCompletedSets guard at :25.
2. await an Activity<WorkoutActivityAttributes>.update(...) for activities matching workoutId, wrapped @MainActor to match the module's convention:

     for activity in Activity<WorkoutActivityAttributes>.activities
     where activity.attributes.workoutId == workoutId {
       await activity.update(ActivityContent(state: newState, staleDate: nil))
     }

No interaction with the module's generation counter — that only guards module-issued Tasks against each other, and JS's authoritative show() lands afterwards regardless.

FinishWorkoutIntent gets NONE of this. Its comment at :93-97 is right: ending the Activity locally would claim a repository write that has not happened. Leave it writing to the outbox and returning.

KNOWN CEILING — mark it in code. Optimism is only corrected while the app is alive. A tap after a force-quit advances the island, and handleWorkoutAction bails at wear-action-task.ts:25 because the in-memory session does not survive process death (active-workout-session.ts:9-10), so the count stays optimistic until the app next runs and drains the outbox. Today that same tap does nothing at all, so this trades one broken behaviour for a narrower one. Leave a 'ponytail:' comment on the optimistic block naming the ceiling and the upgrade path (a liveness marker in the shared store, or dismissing the Activity when no session can be restored).
design: Optimistic fields are only those exactly derivable from (completedSets, totalSets) with no ordering assumption. Segments are not derivable and are left to JS.
acceptance_criteria: performSetAction saves optimistic state and awaits activity.update for matching workoutId; segments and detail carried over unchanged from stored; action derivation matches workout-notification-model.ts:99-108 exactly; FinishWorkoutIntent contains no activity.update; a ponytail: comment names the force-quit ceiling.
close_reason: Closed

title: Retune longCopyPreviewState to a two-digit set count
description:
Every preview content state in apps/mobile/targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivity.swift tops out at totalSets: 9, so the widest count any preview renders is '3/9' — three glyphs. The clipping bug in pump-pal-w9tq only appeared at '0/19', four glyphs. Nothing in the Xcode canvas could have caught it.

Rather than add a new preview state, retune the existing longCopyPreviewState (:331-341) so its numbers are two-digit. It already backs both a lock-screen preview (:400) and the expanded preview (:406), so one edit covers both surfaces:

  static let longCopyPreviewState = ContentState(
    completedSets: 6,
    totalSets: 19,
    detail: "Incline Dumbbell Press · 8 reps · 55 lbs · controlled eccentric tempo",
    segments: [
      .init(sets: 6, started: true, completed: true),
      .init(sets: 8, started: true, completed: false),
      .init(sets: 5, started: false, completed: false),
    ],
    actions: ["completeSet", "uncompleteSet"]
  )

Segments MUST sum to totalSets (6+8+5 = 19). The native module recomputes totalSets from the segment sum rather than trusting the JS value (modules/live-update-notification/ios/LiveUpdateNotificationModule.swift:79), so a preview whose numbers disagree would be lying about production.

Change only the numbers and segments. Keep the detail string and actions array as-is — the state is named longCopy for its long detail string and that intent is unchanged. Add no new #Preview.
acceptance_criteria: longCopyPreviewState has completedSets: 6, totalSets: 19, three segments summing to 19; detail string and actions unchanged; no new #Preview added; the file's #Preview-count assertion still passes.
close_reason: Closed
