title: Narrow Dynamic Island compact pill: ring + set count only
description:
Compact Dynamic Island renders as a full-width pill with a dead centre gap. Root cause: both compactLeading and compactTrailing in apps/mobile/targets/widget/WorkoutLiveActivity.swift end with .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment:). The Dynamic Island sizes the compact pill to its content's intrinsic width, so claiming infinite width forces the pill to maximum; the alignment values only move text inside an already-maximal pill.

Fix (lines 268-288):
- compactLeading: bare ProgressRing(completedSets:totalSets:) with .accessibilityHidden(true). Reuse the existing private ProgressRing at WorkoutLiveActivity.swift:70 (already 16x16, already used by minimal). Do NOT add a new indicator.
- compactTrailing: Text("\(completedSets)/\(totalSets)") with .font(.caption.monospacedDigit()), .lineLimit(1), .minimumScaleFactor(0.8), .accessibilityLabel("Completed sets"), .accessibilityValue("X of Y").
- Delete both .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment:) modifiers. This is the actual fix.
- No replacement .padding — the system already insets compact content.
- Drop the elapsed timer from compact. This INCREASES Android parity: the Pixel analogue is setShortCriticalText, fed exactly \"3/19\" (workout-notification.ios.ts:65), no timer.
- Do NOT touch minimal (289-293), the expanded regions, or the lock-screen view. All chronometers stay unbounded at Date.distantFuture.
design: Compact regions size to intrinsic content width. maxWidth: .infinity is the antipattern. Content parity target is Android's setShortCriticalText chip, not the full notification.
acceptance_criteria: compactLeading contains only ProgressRing; compactTrailing contains only the n/total Text; neither region contains maxWidth: .infinity, .padding, or timerInterval; minimal, expanded regions and lock-screen view are byte-identical to before.
close_reason: Closed

title: Build segments in the active-workout autosave effect
description: app/active-workout.tsx already has a debounced autosave effect (around lines 262-299) that computes 'started' (exercises with a non-empty label) and a flat list of sets, then calls showWorkoutNotification(...). Add the segments field to that existing call: segments: started.map((ex) => ({ sets: ex.sets.length, started: ex.sets.some((s) => s.completed) })). No other call-site changes — app/(tabs)/index.tsx:10 keeps calling dismissWorkoutNotification as-is.
design: Reuse the 'started' array that the effect already builds; do not recompute it or add another effect. Segment order must follow workout order so the ovals read left-to-right in the order the user performs exercises.
acceptance_criteria: showWorkoutNotification receives one segment per named exercise, in workout order, with sets = that exercise's set count and started = whether any of its sets is marked completed; no new effects or renders are introduced; tsc and lint pass.
close_reason: segments built from the existing 'started' array in the autosave effect, workout order preserved, no extra effect or recompute. Zero-length segments are impossible: removeSet guards ex.sets.length <= 1 (hooks/use-draft-exercises.ts:120). tsc now down to only the pre-existing config/firebase.ts error.

title: JS wiring: segments on the shared type, surface selection and fallback latch
description: In utils/workout-notification.ts (the web/iOS no-op stub that owns the shared types), add: export type WorkoutSegment = { sets: number; started: boolean }, and add 'segments: WorkoutSegment[]' to WorkoutNotificationData. Keep every function in that file a no-op. In utils/workout-notification.android.ts, pick a notification surface ONCE per workout and cache it in a module-level 'let useLiveUpdate: boolean | null = null' so the two implementations can never both post and produce a duplicate notification. ensureWorkoutChannel() keeps its current behavior and additionally resolves useLiveUpdate from LiveUpdateNotification.isSupported(). showWorkoutNotification(data) calls the native show() when useLiveUpdate is true; if native show() returns false, latch useLiveUpdate = false and fall through to the existing Notifee call. dismissWorkoutNotification() cancels both paths (idempotent, cheap) and resets useLiveUpdate to null.
design: Keeping utils/workout-notification.android.ts as the single seam means app/active-workout.tsx and app/(tabs)/index.tsx need no knowledge of which surface is in play. The Metro platform-extension split (.android.ts vs .ts) already handles web/iOS, so no Platform.OS checks are needed.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one notification is ever posted for a given workout; a native show() returning false permanently latches that workout to Notifee; dismiss clears both surfaces and resets the latch; the web/iOS stub still type-checks with the new segments field; tsc and lint pass.
close_reason: segments added to the shared type; android surface picks Live Update vs Notifee once per workout and latches to Notifee on native failure. Each path cancels the other before posting, closing the race where ensureWorkoutChannel resolves useLiveUpdate after a refresh already posted via Notifee. Body formatting hoisted to buildNotificationBody and shared by both surfaces.

title: Kotlin: ProgressStyle segments + promoted-ongoing notification
description: Replace the stubs from csx.1 with the real implementation in LiveUpdateNotificationModule.kt. isSupported() returns Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 36 && notificationManager.canPostPromotedNotifications(). show(payload) builds a framework android.app.Notification.Builder (NOT NotificationCompat) on the existing 'active-workout' channel and posts it, returning notification.hasPromotableCharacteristics() so JS can fall back when false. dismiss() cancels the notification id. Payload from JS: title, text, startedAtMillis, shortCriticalText, progress (completed set count), and segments: Array<{sets: Int, started: Boolean}>.
design: Builder configuration: Notification.ProgressStyle() with setProgressSegments(segments.map { Notification.ProgressStyle.Segment(it.sets).setColor(if (it.started) 0xFFE54242.toInt() else 0xFF555555.toInt()) }), setProgress(completedSetCount), setStyledByProgress(false) so each segment keeps its own color instead of being recolored by tracker position. Plus setOngoing(true), setCategory(Notification.CATEGORY_PROGRESS), setWhen(startedAtMillis), setUsesChronometer(true), setShortCriticalText(...), setSmallIcon via resources.getIdentifier("ic_stat_timber", "drawable", packageName) since the module has its own R class, setContentTitle/setContentText, content intent = the app launcher intent, and extras.putBoolean(Notification.EXTRA_REQUEST_PROMOTED_ONGOING, true). Colors #e54242 / #555 come from app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:9-10. Promotion disqualifiers that must be avoided: custom RemoteViews, setColorized(true), setGroupSummary(true), or an IMPORTANCE_MIN channel — reuse the existing DEFAULT-importance 'active-workout' channel. Guard all API 36 calls behind a version check so the module still compiles and runs on older devices.
acceptance_criteria: Kotlin compiles against compileSdk 36; isSupported() correctly gates on API level and canPostPromotedNotifications(); show() returns false rather than throwing when the built notification is not promotable; no promotion disqualifier is set; dismiss() cancels cleanly.
close_reason: Kotlin ProgressStyle + promoted-ongoing implemented. All API-36 signatures verified against ~/Android/Sdk/platforms/android-36/android.jar via javap. EXTRA_REQUEST_PROMOTED_ONGOING is android-36.1-only so the literal key 'android.requestPromotedOngoing' is used instead — no compileSdk bump. Failures log to logcat and return false so JS latches to Notifee.

title: Generate ic_stat_timber drawables and set smallIcon on the Notifee path
description: No status-bar small icon is currently shipped: there is no ic_stat_* drawable in the generated res folder and utils/workout-notification.android.ts sets no smallIcon, so Notifee falls back to ic_launcher and Android renders it as a white blob. This matters more for Live Updates because the status-bar chip and the AOD both draw the small icon. Write a one-off Node script using sharp (already in node_modules) that reads assets/images/android-icon-monochrome.png, trims the adaptive-icon safe-zone padding, forces white-on-transparent, and emits ic_stat_timber.png at 24/36/48/72/96 px into modules/live-update-notification/android/src/main/res/drawable-{mdpi,hdpi,xhdpi,xxhdpi,xxxhdpi}/. Module resources merge into the app at build time, so no config plugin and no touching the gitignored android/. Then set smallIcon: 'ic_stat_timber' on the notifee.displayNotification call in utils/workout-notification.android.ts and delete the now-stale 'ponytail:' comment about the missing small icon (around line 47).
design: Do NOT reuse mipmap/ic_launcher_monochrome directly — it carries adaptive-icon safe-zone padding and would render undersized in the status bar. Keep the generator script in the repo (scripts/) so the drawables can be regenerated if the source icon changes.
acceptance_criteria: Five ic_stat_timber.png files exist under the module's res drawable-* folders, white-on-transparent with padding trimmed; utils/workout-notification.android.ts passes smallIcon: 'ic_stat_timber'; the stale ponytail comment is gone; lint and tsc pass.
close_reason: ic_stat_timber.png generated at 24/36/48/72/96px into the module's drawable-* folders by scripts/generate-ic-stat-timber.js. Verified independently: all five have correct dimensions and non-uniform alpha (min 0 / max 255 / mean ~133), so no solid-block regression. Source trim was 672x612 of 1024x1024, confirming real safe-zone padding removed. smallIcon wired into the Notifee call; stale ponytail comment deleted.

title: Scaffold live-update-notification Expo module + promoted-notifications permission
description: Create a local Expo module at modules/live-update-notification via 'npx create-expo-module --local live-update-notification', then strip the generated iOS, web, and View scaffolding — this is Android-only. Expose three functions from the TS wrapper and the Kotlin module: isSupported(): boolean, show(payload): boolean, dismiss(): void. In THIS bead all three are stubs: isSupported() returns false, show() returns false, dismiss() is a no-op. Also add 'android.permission.POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS' to expo.android.permissions in app.json, next to the existing POST_NOTIFICATIONS.

Do not touch android/ — it is gitignored (.gitignore:49) and regenerated by prebuild. Module Kotlin package should match the app package convention (com.aquinnmo.timber.liveupdate).
acceptance_criteria: modules/live-update-notification exists with an Android-only Kotlin module and TS wrapper exporting isSupported/show/dismiss; no iOS or web files remain; app.json lists POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS; npx tsc --noEmit and npm run lint both pass; app behavior is unchanged (Notifee path still used).

Uses requireOptionalNativeModule so pre-existing dev clients without the native module return false rather than crashing. lint clean; only tsc error is pre-existing in config/firebase.ts.

title: Pixel AOD Live Update notification for active workouts
description: Post an Android 16 Live Update (promoted ongoing) notification during an active workout, so it appears in the status-bar chip, on the lock screen, and on the Pixel Always-On Display. Progress bar uses Notification.ProgressStyle with one oval per exercise, length proportional to that exercise's set count, grey (#555) until the exercise has at least one completed set, then fully red (#e54242). Falls back to the existing Notifee ongoing notification when the OS does not allow promotion (pre-API 36, or user disabled promoted notifications). Notifee 9.1.8 has no ProgressStyle support, so this needs a local Expo native module.
design: Local Expo module under modules/ (android/ is gitignored, CNG project). Framework Notification.Builder + Notification.ProgressStyle, not NotificationCompat, to avoid pinning an androidx.core version for setRequestPromotedOngoing. compileSdk/targetSdk already default to 36 in Expo 54, so no Gradle changes. POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS goes in app.json android.permissions, no config plugin. Existing utils/workout-notification.android.ts stays the single seam; it picks a surface once per workout and latches to Notifee on failure so the two paths can never both post.
acceptance_criteria: On an Android 16 Pixel: starting a workout shows a promoted ongoing notification with one grey oval per exercise sized by set count; completing any set of an exercise turns that entire oval red; the notification renders on lock screen and AOD with a legible small icon; finish/discard removes it. On a device without promotion support, the existing Notifee notification appears instead, with no crash and no duplicate.

title: Promote App Check to enforce on preview then production
description:
security_report.md finding 3 proper. wrangler.toml:17 and :30 both set APP_CHECK_MODE=monitor. Local enforce is handled separately (pump-pal-wa2h); this is the deploy-wide promotion.

docs/deployment.md:88-98 defines a human gate: 24h of 100 percent verified telemetry, a documented owner, and a tested rollback. The local work supplies evidence but does not satisfy the gate. security_report.md:629 additionally wants a deployment check that rejects missing, invalid, or unknown APP_CHECK_MODE values - worker.ts:127 currently compares === 'enforce', so every other value including a typo is fail-open.

Order: preview first, soak, then production. Rollback is setting the var back to monitor (docs/deployment.md:136-138).

Effect: tokens still mint, but iOS silently degrades to DeviceCheck - weaker attestation than intended. Needs an Expo config plugin (apps/mobile/plugins/) or an app.json entitlements entry.

title: Route callAI through apiRequestCore

Consolidating means apiRequestCore has to accommodate the AI-specific error handling it knows nothing about: AIQuotaError, recordRemaining on 429, AIDisabledError, AIOfflineError, and the Vercel-shaped { error: { code, message } } body parsing. Not urgent - file separately so the enforce work stays small.
acceptance_criteria: callAI shares one request seam with the domain REST client, with the AI-specific 429/quota/offline behavior preserved.

Grants a larger Live Activity update budget when the user leaves frequent updates enabled in Settings. Not a substitute for the other beads - it only widens the margin for a long workout. One key, no code.
acceptance_criteria:
- apps/mobile/app.json expo.ios.infoPlist contains NSSupportsLiveActivitiesFrequentUpdates: true.
- bun run test passes.
close_reason: Implemented and verified locally; parent device acceptance remains outstanding.

title: Android pays the same duplicate Live Activity show() per tap
description:
Out of scope for the iOS latency work (pump-pal-jcgl), filed so it is not lost.

The duplicate-draw cause is platform-agnostic: app/active-workout.tsx:431 is a 100ms setTimeout effect that re-fires whenever 'exercises' changes, so a notification-button tap produces one immediate show() from src/lib/wear-action-task.ts:35 plus a second identical one 100ms later. pump-pal-jcgl fixes this only in src/lib/workout-notification.ios.ts.

src/lib/workout-notification.android.ts has no equivalent dedupe, so Android still posts the promoted ongoing notification twice per tap. Decide whether to mirror the lastPayloadKey guard there or hoist the dedupe to a shared layer — the two files are platform variants resolved by extension, so there is no shared module today, which is why the iOS fix was kept local.

Verify against the Android path first: Notification.ProgressStyle updates may be cheap enough that this is waste rather than user-visible lag.
acceptance_criteria: Either the dedupe is mirrored in workout-notification.android.ts, or a measurement shows the duplicate post is harmless on Android and this is closed with that finding recorded.

title: Drop profile.aiUsage from the client profile DTO

The field is still decoded and synced for no reader: packages/contract/src/api-contract.ts:76,81, apps/mobile/src/types/user.ts:52, apps/mobile/src/data/sync.ts:68, apps/mobile/src/data/profile-repository.web.ts:27, apps/mobile/src/data/firestore-sync-remote.ts decodeProfile (3 call sites). Removing it also drops a per-profile-read Firestore GET of users/{uid}/private/aiUsage. Server-side apps/api/src/store/profile.ts may keep it or not — check whether anything still consumes ProfileDTO.aiUsage first.
acceptance_criteria: No client or contract reference to profile.aiUsage remains; firestore-sync-remote no longer fetches the private aiUsage doc on profile reads; all four test groups pass.

Fires once during app boot, before the sync errors. Source component not yet identified. Pre-existing, surfaced while verifying the workspace split.
